2027-03-02.title: Fourth Tuesday of the Great Fast
2027-03-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: That all may honour the Son
2027-03-02.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-03-02.verse: So it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.
theo: Yesterday Abram set out in faith; today, a few verses later, he is afraid. “Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to reside there as an alien.” At the border he makes a plan to save his own skin: “Say you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and that my life may be spared on your account.” The father of faith tells a half-lie, and Sarai pays for it: she is taken into Pharaoh's house. It is the pagan king who has to rebuke the man of God: “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?” Scripture does not polish its heroes. Faith is not a straight line from call to glory; it stumbles, it is afraid, it uses others to protect itself. And yet God does not abandon the promise or the woman who carries it: “the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.” There is a word here for every marriage. Fear can make a husband or a wife sacrifice the other to save themselves; God stands on the side of the one who is sacrificed.

The second reading follows the confession of Achan. Israel had been routed at Ai; now the sin has been brought into the light, and God speaks again: “Do not fear or be dismayed; take all the fighting men with you, and go up now to Ai.” The place of defeat becomes the place of a new beginning. These battle stories belong to a hard and ancient world, and the Church does not read them as a pattern for treating any people; the Fathers read them as pictures of our own struggle against sin. Read that way, the lesson is clear and consoling. After a fall and a good confession, God does not send us somewhere easier. He sends us back to the same Ai, the same temptation, the same weak place, but now he goes with us.

Paul faces a hard question: if God chooses, is God unjust? “By no means!” he answers, and quotes the word God spoke to Moses: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.” Then comes the sentence that stands over the whole Great Fast: “So it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.” Our fasting is not wasted effort, but it is not a payment either. We fast to make room for a mercy we could never earn. In the Gospel Jesus reveals where that mercy comes from: “the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.” The Father “loves the Son and shows him all that he himself is doing”, and has given him the power to give life and to judge, “so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.” This is the faith of the Church: Jesus is not merely a good teacher but the eternal Son, one with the Father. That is why, at the Holy Qurbana, we bow before him and adore.
outline: Ask: when I am afraid, whom do I sacrifice to save myself?
Point 1 · Say you are my sister
The father of faith afraid in Egypt.
Point 2 · Go up now to Ai
Back to the place of defeat, with God.
Not exertion but mercy, revealed in the Son.
“It depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.”
live: Correct one half-truth you have told, at home or at work, before the week is out.
Identify the place where you usually fall, and plan with God one concrete change for that place.
2027-03-02.prayer: Merciful Father, Abram was afraid and you kept your promise; Israel was defeated and you sent them out again. Do not look on our fears and our half-truths, but on your mercy. Teach us to honour your Son as we honour you, and to do what we see him doing. Lead us back to the places where we fell, and walk there with us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we honour the Son as we honour the Father: we adore him present on the altar, and receive from him the life the Father has given him to give.

quick: Abram, afraid in Egypt, lied about Sarai; God protected her and kept his promise.
After confession, God sent Israel back to Ai: “Do not fear or be dismayed.”
Everything depends on God who shows mercy; the Son does what he sees the Father doing.
2027-03-02.action: Correct one half-truth you have told.
2027-03-02.question: When I am afraid, whom do I put at risk to protect myself?

family.explain: Abram was a great friend of God, but once he was very afraid. He asked his wife Sarai to tell a lie so that he would be safe. God protected Sarai anyway. Even good people make mistakes when they are afraid. God wants us to tell the truth and trust him.
family.intention: We pray for husbands and wives, that they may always protect each other.
family.ask: Ask: “When are we tempted to tell a small lie because we are afraid? What could we do instead?”

illus: A young clerk in a bank in Thodupuzha made a small error in an account and covered it with a false entry. The false entry needed another, and soon he could not sleep. During the Lenten retreat he went to confession, and the priest told him gently that the confession was not finished until he told his manager. He went the next morning expecting to lose his job. The manager listened, corrected the entries with him, and said only: “Now I know I can trust you.”

pm.open: Lord, you show mercy to whom you will. We come with our fears and our failures; have mercy on us. Amen.
share: Say you are my sister (Genesis 12:13). Where has fear made me deceive or use someone?
Do not fear or be dismayed; go up now to Ai (Joshua 8:1). What place of defeat is God asking me to face again?
It depends on God who shows mercy (Romans 9:16). Do I treat my fast as a payment or as an opening to mercy?
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mercy of God to all.
For husbands and wives, that fear may never make them betray one another.
For those who have fallen, that they may rise and try again.
For those who do not yet honour the Son, that they may come to know him.
For our group, that we may speak the truth in love.
pm.close: Father, everything depends on your mercy. Free us from fear, make us truthful, and teach us to do what we see your Son doing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Abram, who left everything in faith, becomes afraid in Egypt. He tells his wife: say you are my sister, so that my life may be spared (Genesis 12:13). The father of faith tells a half-lie, and Sarai pays the price. But God protects her and keeps his promise.

After Achan's confession, God says to Joshua: do not fear or be dismayed; go up now to Ai (Joshua 8:1). God sends him back to the very place of defeat. After a good confession, God often sends us back to the same weak place, but now he goes with us.
Paul says: it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy (Romans 9:16). Our fast does not buy God's mercy; it opens our hearts to receive it.

Jesus says: the Son does whatever he sees the Father doing, so that all may honour the Son just as they honour the Father (John 5:19, 23). Let us honour him today, at the altar and in our lives, and do what we see him doing. Amen.
kids: Children, Abram was afraid and told a lie, but God still took care of everyone. When you are afraid, do not tell a lie: tell Jesus you are afraid, and tell the truth. He will help you!

intro: Theme: “So it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.”
Abram's fear in Egypt, Israel sent back to Ai, the mercy of God, and the Son who does what the Father does.

sub: God protects the one who is sacrificed.
q: Say you are my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and that my life may be spared on your account.
So then, putting away falsehood, let all of us speak the truth to our neighbors, for we are members of one another.
points.apply: Correct one half-truth this week, especially one that has hurt someone close to you.

sub: Back to the weak place, with God.
q: Then the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not fear or be dismayed; take all the fighting men with you, and go up now to Ai.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Name the place where you usually fall, and plan one change there with prayer.

sub: Is there injustice with God? By no means.
The Son does what the Father does.
q: I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.
So it depends not on human will or exertion, but on God who shows mercy.
points.apply: Offer your fast today not as a payment but as thanksgiving for mercy received.

concl: Our heroes stumble, our battles are lost and won again, and everything rests on mercy.
The Son shows us the Father's face: honour him, and do what you see him doing.
2027-03-02.resolve: This week, tell the truth where fear has made you hide it, and thank God each night for one mercy received.
